jobs.excerpt: OleOle is seeking a Director of Strategic Finance to build and own the financial model behind a global football platform with multiple interconnected businesses.
jobs.description:
OleOle is seeking a Director of Strategic Finance to build and own the financial model behind a global football platform with multiple interconnected businesses.

This is not a traditional accounting or controllership role. We are looking for someone who can take a complex platform strategy and translate it into a rigorous, investor-grade financial model that demonstrates how OleOle’s businesses develop individually and collectively as the platform scales.

Your first major responsibility will be building the OleOle master financial model. The model will examine the business at approximately 50 million, 100 million and 400 million global users, allowing assumptions around adoption, engagement, transaction volume, pricing, margins and penetration to change dynamically across the ecosystem.

You will build detailed economic models for OleOleSport ticketing, travel and VIP hospitality; Bad Monkey, our planned hybrid fixed-odds and prediction-market gaming business; Mini Programs and third-party commerce; sponsorship and commercial partnerships; and NewZeros, OleOle’s planned financial infrastructure encompassing payments, wallets, transaction processing and exchange capabilities.

NewZeros represents a particularly important long-term opportunity. The model must go beyond conventional exchange economics to examine what happens if OleOle’s financial infrastructure participates in payments and transactions generated throughout an ecosystem serving tens or potentially hundreds of millions of users.

OleOleSport requires a different approach. Because ticketing, travel and hospitality can potentially generate revenue before OleOle develops a large social audience, you will build a detailed bottom-up model for this business and help demonstrate its role as an early commercial engine.

You will also model OleOle’s capital requirements, cash utilization, operating expenses, unit economics, gross margins and long-term profitability. The objective is not to manufacture aggressive revenue projections. It is to create a defensible model in which management and investors can change assumptions and immediately understand their effect on the business.

You will work directly with the Founder & CEO and, as the company grows, with our CFO and business-unit leadership. The financial model you create will become a permanent management and fundraising tool and will evolve as actual operating data replaces assumptions.

Following funding, this role will continue as a senior member of OleOle’s finance organization, owning strategic planning, forecasting, budgeting, business-unit economics, KPI development, scenario analysis and financial reporting while helping build the company’s broader finance function.

We are looking for someone with exceptional financial modeling and analytical ability who understands how to model businesses such as marketplaces, payments, fintech, exchanges, gaming, consumer platforms or other transaction-driven businesses. Experience in investment banking, strategic finance, growth-stage technology, private equity, venture-backed companies or similarly rigorous financial environments would be particularly relevant.

The right person must be comfortable starting with ambiguity. OleOle is creating businesses that do not fit neatly into a conventional SaaS model. You will be expected to understand how each economic engine actually works, challenge assumptions, identify missing variables and construct the financial framework from the ground up.

This is ultimately the person who turns our vision into numbers sophisticated investors can interrogate.

OleOle is currently being built by a team working under deferred compensation while we complete our funding. This is not an unpaid or volunteer position: compensation is agreed upon in writing and accrues during the deferred period, becoming payable following funding. Once funded, this role will transition to a traditional compensation structure including a competitive salary, equity ownership and participation in the OleX token program. We are looking for someone who understands the realities of building an ambitious company before institutional funding and wants to remain with OleOle as the company grows.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in strategic finance, investment banking, private equity, growth equity, corporate development, venture-backed technology, fintech, payments, marketplaces, gaming, exchanges or other transaction-driven businesses.
  • Exceptional financial modeling skills, with demonstrated experience building complex, multi-business operating models from the ground up rather than maintaining models created by others.
  • Experience building integrated financial models encompassing revenue drivers, unit economics, transaction volume, gross margin, operating expenses, cash flow, capital requirements, scenario analysis and long-term profitability.
  • Demonstrated ability to model businesses at significant scale, including scenarios involving tens or hundreds of millions of users, large transaction volumes, multiple geographies and multiple interconnected revenue streams.
  • Deep understanding of payments and financial-network economics, including transaction volume, take rates, basis-point economics, merchant payments, wallets, cross-border transactions, payment-processing costs and network effects.
  • Strong understanding of marketplace and platform economics, including GMV, buyer/seller participation, merchant adoption, transaction frequency, take rates, contribution margins and network effects.
  • Experience with exchange or trading economics, including trading volume, liquidity, spreads, transaction fees and the economics of operating financial marketplaces.
  • Experience with gaming, sports betting or prediction-market economics is highly desirable, particularly an understanding of fixed-odds betting, hold, liquidity, market making, prediction markets, gaming taxes and jurisdiction-specific economics.
  • Experience evaluating or modeling consumer internet/social platforms at substantial scale, including user acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, cohort behavior and monetization.
  • Ability to build sophisticated scenario models in which assumptions can be dynamically changed and flow through individual business units and consolidated company financials.
  • Demonstrated experience producing financial models and investment materials capable of withstanding scrutiny from institutional investors, venture capital firms, private equity firms, investment banks, family offices and sophisticated financial counterparties.
  • Experience supporting significant capital raises, M&A transactions, strategic investments, IPO preparation or institutional financing is strongly preferred.
  • Ability to translate an ambitious strategic vision into measurable financial assumptions without confusing opportunity with forecast. Must be comfortable challenging founders and senior executives when assumptions cannot be financially supported.
  • Strong understanding of three-statement financial modeling, valuation methodologies, discounted cash flow analysis, comparable-company analysis, sensitivity analysis, capital structure and financing scenarios.
  • Advanced Excel and/or Google Sheets modeling skills are essential. Experience using SQL, Python, BI platforms, financial planning systems or AI-assisted financial analysis is highly desirable.
  • MBA, CFA, CPA or advanced degree in finance, economics, accounting or a quantitative discipline preferred. Exceptional professional experience may substitute for formal credentials.
  • Previous experience at a leading investment bank, private equity/growth equity firm, major fintech/payments company, global technology platform or highly successful venture-backed company would be particularly attractive.
  • Experience working internationally and modeling businesses across multiple currencies, regulatory environments and geographic markets is strongly preferred.
  • Must be capable of working directly with the Founder & CEO and senior technical/product leadership in an early-stage environment where significant portions of the business are still being designed.
  • Must be willing to personally build the model. This is not a role for someone who has reached the point in their career where all detailed financial analysis is delegated to analysts.

Solutions not problems .

  • Creative problem solver who can courageously propose and support new ideas to our organization. Not interested in best practices, lets build something better!
  • Ability to adapt. An ideal candidate will welcome the opportunity to solve a broad range of problems using a wide array of technologies.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities and general growing pains of an early-stage technology company
  • An exceptional entrepreneurial judgment that fosters independence over micro-management
  • Understanding of football and international sports a huge plus

Ole Ole is located in beautiful Austin Texas, however, this role requires some travel we are privately held and rapidly growing!

OleOle is building a global social, messaging and commerce platform designed specifically for the more than three billion football fans around the world.

The platform brings together social media, short-form video, encrypted messaging and calling, live scores, real-time translation and football content within a single global ecosystem. Our goal is to connect fans across clubs, countries and languages while creating an infrastructure that extends well beyond social media.

Every OleOle user receives a persistent Wallet ID that connects their identity across the ecosystem. Over time, OleOle will integrate payments, commerce, Mini Programs, ticketing and travel, gaming, digital assets and financial services. Mini Programs will allow clubs, brands, merchants and third-party developers to build services directly within OleOle, using the platform’s identity, social and payment infrastructure.

OleOleSport, our ticketing and travel business, provides an important early commercial opportunity through tickets, VIP hospitality and travel experiences around major sporting events. As the OleOle audience grows, additional businesses are designed to scale alongside it, including Mini Programs, payments, gaming and NewZeros, our planned financial infrastructure combining exchange capabilities with a broader payments and transaction network.

We are currently a team of approximately 20 people building across backend infrastructure, social, video, messaging, AI and translation, payments, football data, product and design.

OleOle is being built around a long-term thesis: football is the world’s largest shared passion, yet its global audience remains fragmented across social networks, messaging applications, sports platforms and commerce providers. We believe there is an opportunity to bring those experiences together in one global platform and build significant businesses around the resulting network.

jobs.excerpt: Boosters — це українська продуктова компанія.  Ми створюємо глобальні продукти в сферах Productivity та EdTech, які несуть цінність для 60 мільйонів людей.
jobs.description:
Boosters — це українська продуктова компанія. Ми створюємо глобальні продукти в сферах Productivity та EdTech, які несуть цінність для 60 мільйонів людей. Для нас важливо будувати продукти з довготривалим впливом — системні, масштабні та здатні залишатися актуальними десятиліттями.

Зараз ми шукаємо Head of Engineering в наш флагманський продукт JustDone — AI асистент для академічної аудиторії, який допомагає краще працювати з науковими роботами, навчатись і проводити глибинні дослідження. Ми віримо, що AI може суттєво змінити те, як люди навчаються та працюють з інформацією. Не через cheating, а через якісніший і глибший рісьорч, швидшу роботу з великими обсягами інформації та автоматизацію формальних і рутинних задач. Так у студентів і дослідників залишається більше часу на те, що справді має значення — мислення, навчання та власні ідеї.

Основна мета цієї ролі — побудувати engineering-функцію, яка дозволяє JustDone швидко експериментувати й шипити продуктові зміни, водночас зберігаючи стабільність ключових систем.

Сьогодні JustDone це

  • 3+ млн преміум користувачів;
  • #1 позиція в США в ніші AI Writing Assistants;
  • 90%+ одиниць контенту, створених користувачами, знаходять реальне застосування;
  • понад 3 млн одиниць контенту, який генерується користувачами щомісяця;
  • власні AI та NLP рішення: AI Detector, Text Humanization Engines, AI Research Assistant.

Твоє майбутнє середовище

Наша головна перевага — це люди. Ми працюємо з тими, хто щодня прагне до самовдосконалення та задає високу планку гри.

Лідер напрямку — Роман Гмиря, COO. Він цінує відкриту й зрозумілу комунікацію, швидкість у прийнятті рішень та здоровий прагматизм — уміння знаходити рішення, які найкраще працюють для продукту й команди.

Саме в цій ролі ти отримаєш

  • Повний технічний оунершип над продуктом, що вже має трекшн;
  • Сильну команду поруч — працюватимеш з лідерами напрямків: NLP Lead, Lead Product Manager, Lead Product Designer, Lead Product Manager.
  • Прямий вплив на команду з 15 скілових інженерів, архітектуру і стратегію;
  • Філософію та умови для твого постійного росту та розвитку;
  • Великий простір для втілення власних ідей і впливу на продукт.

Твоя зона впливу

  • Переклад бізнес-стратегії у чіткий технічний роадмап і реалізація його у вигляді систем, коду та результатів;
  • Прийняття ключових архітектурних рішень для вебу, native apps (desktop, mobile) та браузерних розширень (React, Next.js, Go, Postgres, AWS, AI-стек);
  • Розвиток AI-native інженерії;
  • Лідерство інженерної команди: код-рев’ю, менторство, допомога в адаптації нових інженерів, допомога в пріоритизації;
  • People management задачі: проведення 1:1, онбординг нових гравців, розробка PDP планів;
  • Побудова ефективної взаємодії з NLP, продуктовою, дизайн-командою та growth-напрямком;
  • Відповідальність за надійність інфраструктури та налаштування DevOps-процесів.

Для цього тобі знадобиться

  • 7+ років технічного досвіду (пріоритет — back-end розробка), з них щонайменше 2 роки у ролі Team Lead / Engineering Manager / Head of Engineering або на співставній позиції.
  • Досвід управління engineering-командами від 10 людей.
  • Сильна технічна база та глибоке розуміння архітектури web і mobile продуктів.
  • Глибокі знання в архітектурі веб та мобільних застосунків: React.js, Web SPA (платформа), Next.js; Go + PostgresDB +AWS + AI стек;
  • Практичний досвід з AI/ML/NLP: впровадження моделей, робота з LLM та інтеграціями через API.
  • Розуміння та практичний досвід із CI/CD, Docker і DevOps practices.
  • Досвід роботи у продуктових компаніях або стартапах, що проходили етап швидкого масштабування.
  • Англійська на рівні B2+.

Твій шлях до команди Boosters

Pre-screen з рекрутером (45 хвилин) → Інтервʼю з СOО → Кейсове інтервʼю з Lead NLP Engineer → Bar-raising (1 година)

Ми пропонуємо

Кар’єрний та персональний розвиток

  • Планові performance review і розробка PDP;
  • Підтримка в розвитку твого персонального бренду в соцмережах Boosters і експертних медіа;
  • Профільні комʼюніті Genesis з безкоштовними курсами і можливістю нетворкінгу;
  • Бюджет на курси, конференції та вивчення англійської;
  • Техніка від компанії та оплата всіх необхідних сервісів для роботи.

Автономію та гнучкість

  • Можливість обирати між роботою в офісі (Київ або Львів) та remote-first форматом (Україна та закордон);
  • Гнучкий старт дня (з 8 до 11 ранку за Києвом);
  • 20 дей-офів на рік, вихідні на державні свята та безлімітні лікарняні.

Турботу про здоров’я

  • Медичне страхування;
  • Компенсація роботи з психологом;
  • Індивідуальний бенефіт на заняття спортом;
  • Сніданки й обіди (on-site в офісах);
  • Спортивні активності Genesis: спільнота для бігу, волейбол, йога (офлайн); стретчинг та йога (онлайн).

jobs.description:
Job Description:

The Fractional Controller directs and supports the accounting and financial activities of client companies that do not require a full-time internal accounting department or Chief Financial Officer. This role is responsible for overseeing the preparation and analysis of current financial information, developing forecasts and budgets, maintaining financial controls, and supporting strategic and operational decision-making. The Fractional Controller works closely with client leadership, internal CFOs, and accounting staff under varying project structures. This position can be based in any Frost, PLLC office location or can be fully remote.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • May supervise or guide client accounting staff on an as-needed basis.
  • Collaborates with internal CFO and advisory teams.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Work with clients and internal teams to develop short-, mid-, and long-term financial forecasts.
  • Prepare budgets based on forecasts and business objectives.
  • Assist with and oversee month-end and year-end close processes.
  • Reconcile bank accounts and review general ledger activity.
  • Direct the preparation of financial statements, including income statements, balance sheets, and related reports.
  • Compare sales and profit projections to actual results and budgeted expenses to actual expenses; recommend or implement adjustments to forecasts and budgets.
  • Provide strategic management of accounting and finance functions for clients.
  • Develop, implement, and improve accounting policies, procedures, internal controls, and financial manuals.
  • Recommend improvements to ensure the accuracy, integrity, and reliability of financial information.
  • Implement and optimize accounting systems; assist with conversions and upgrades as needed.
  • Provide cost accounting and margin analysis to support understanding of product and service profitability.
  • Identify and manage business risks, including insurance requirements.
  • Review financial planning processes and suggest improvements to current methods.
  • Oversee or support the investment of funds and assist with capital raises or expansion initiatives, working with investment bankers as required.
  • Collaborate with client executive leadership and management on financial strategy and operational planning.
  • Assist clients with hiring efforts related to accounting and finance functions.
  • Support preparation of financial reports required for shareholders, lenders, regulatory bodies, or other stakeholders.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Required Skills and Abilities:

  • BS in Accounting or Professional Accountancy.
  • At least 7-10 years of accounting experience.
  • Travel approximately 25% of time.
  • Remote work availability.

Nice To Have Experience:

  • CPA or CMA preferred but not required.

  • Professional Memberships: We cover fees for business, civic, and professional organizations.
  • Well-being Resources: Support for your emotional well-being.
  • Life and Disability Insurance: Peace of mind with our paid insurance programs.
  • Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave.
  • CPE Memberships: We cover your membership fees to state CPA societies and the AICPA.
  • Paid CPE: Continuous professional education on us.

What Can You Expect?

  • Initial Screening: A phone call to understand your fit for the role.

  • Feedback Loop: Transparent communication throughout the hiring process.

Frost CFO Services provides a better solution for the role of the chief financial officer, offering a dynamic array of outsources financial and accounting services to fill transitional gaps, lower operating costs, and improve business efficiency.

jobs.description:
Recruiting Firm, Riderflex has been hired by our client, TinyMobileRobots, to find their Territory Manager for upstate New York!

Job Title: Territory ManagerReports to: Regional Sales Director, East US & CanadaDepartment: SalesNumber of Direct Reports: 0Status: Full-time, RemotePay Range: $70,000 base salary, plus 5% commission and annual bonus potentialLocation: Upstate New York. Remote and home-based, with regular travel throughout the territory.

COMPANY OVERVIEW

TinyMobileRobots builds autonomous robots that paint the lines on sports fields. One person and one robot can stripe a football field in a fraction of the time it takes a crew with a walk-behind striper. Headquartered in Kennesaw, Georgia, the company sells and services its robots across the United States and Canada to school districts, municipalities, parks and recreation departments, colleges and universities, professional teams, and youth sports organizations.

The company is growing about 30% a year and has moved past the startup stage, with a company-wide sales methodology in place and an inside sales team that sets demonstrations for the field. The culture is light, competitive, and fun. The people who thrive here can walk onto a high school football field, pull a robot out of the back of a truck, and turn a demonstration into a show.

Is this you?

  • Passionate about sports
  • Ultra-competitive and loves to win
  • Loves technology and the freedom to operate in an entrepreneurial company
  • Accomplished B2B sales professional with value-based selling experience
  • Committed to driving exceptional customer success and maximizing long-term client value

Does this sound like what you have been looking for?

POSITION SUMMARY

The Territory Manager owns revenue and brand awareness for TinyMobileRobots throughout upstate New York. This is classic, home-based direct sales: build the pipeline, book the demonstrations, get in the vehicle, run the demo on the field, close the deal, then install and train so the customer becomes a reference. It is a blend of front-line selling and customer success, and it takes a self-motivated hunter who also works well with the team behind them.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

A. Build and Work the Pipeline

  • Prospect daily and self-source new opportunities across the territory. Marketing and inside sales will send leads and set some demonstrations, but filling the funnel is the job.
  • Follow up on every inbound demo request and inquiry, qualify the opportunity, and get it on the calendar.
  • Plan territory coverage and travel so one trip reaches several prospects, not one.
  • Keep every deal current in HubSpot so forecasting is accurate.

B. Sell in the Field

  • Run compelling on-site demonstrations for individuals and groups, typically about two hours, on grass and synthetic turf.
  • Navigate the whole customer organization, from the grounds crew member who will operate the robot, to the grounds supervisor, to the athletic director or administrator who approves the purchase.
  • Sell on value, not price. Hold the line on pricing and lead with what the robot does for the customer.
  • Manage the full sales cycle, including RFPs, competitive bids, and accurate, policy-compliant quotations.
  • Represent the company at regional trade shows and field days, and support national exhibitions as needed.

C. Grow the Account

  • Sell the full line: paint, nozzle and maintenance kits, accessories, and extended warranties. These are meaningful revenue for the company and for you.
  • Manage the installation and customer training so every new customer is set up to succeed.
  • Turn happy customers into reference customers and referral sources.
  • Get customers to service and support quickly when they need it, rather than letting an issue wait.

D. Know the Market

  • Maintain expert-level knowledge of the customer base, the competition, and the tactics competitors use in your pipeline, and counter them.
  • Understand the different types of fields, environments, and field maintenance processes your customers deal with every day.

QUALIFICATIONS

A. Education

Degree from an accredited college or university, or related work experience. No robotics or sports industry background required.

B. Experience

  • Three to five or more years of direct sales with a demonstrated history of meeting and exceeding quota in a defined geographic territory.
  • A hunter. You have found and closed your own business, even if that was a prior role.
  • Tenure. You have stayed and succeeded in your sales roles rather than moving every year or two.
  • Working knowledge of a CRM and the sales cycle inside it. HubSpot is a plus, not a requirement.
  • Selling to institutional buyers with budget cycles, such as schools, municipalities, or government, is helpful but not required.

C. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Strong persuasion, presentation, negotiation, and listening skills, verbal and written.
  • Builds sound plans, executes them, and adjusts, with solid financial and business judgment.
  • Customer-centric mindset that creates loyalty.
  • Confident without being a know-it-all. Asks for help, shares what works, and listens more than lectures.
  • Technology savvy, with basic knowledge of hardware, software, firmware, wireless and cellular.
  • Comfortable using AI tools for research and prospecting.

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS

  • Home-based with regular driving throughout the territory, often over extended distances, and 30 to 50 overnight nights per year.
  • Must reside in upstate New York.
  • Ability to lift up to 100 pounds at any given time. The largest robot is 77 pounds and paint is 55 pounds per box, plus toolkit and supplies.
  • Vehicle capable of transporting the robots: a midsize SUV or larger, a midsize pickup or larger, or a van. Candidates without one must be willing to obtain one upon hire.
  • Protected, lockable space at home to store two robots and supplies.
  • Frequently outdoors in rain, heat, humidity, dirt and mud, and uneven or sloped terrain.
  • Valid driver's license, and must pass a motor vehicle report and a substance abuse test.
  • Fluency in English required, bilingual preferred.

COMPENSATION

  • Base salary starting at $70,000 annually
  • 5% commission on everything sold, including robots, accessories, paint, and warranty services
  • Annual bonus program

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) program
  • 13 days of paid time off, 11 paid holidays, and your birthday off
  • Mileage reimbursement and a travel and expense budget
  • Work from home with a flexible schedule

jobs.companyName: Americans United for Separation of Church and State
jobs.description:
Americans United for Separation of Church and State is seeking full-time summer legal interns who are committed to civil rights, impact litigation, and upholding core First Amendment protections.

About Americans United. Americans United is a nonpartisan educational and advocacy organization dedicated to advancing the constitutional principle of church-state separation as the only way to ensure freedom of religion, including the right to believe or not believe, for all of us. Founded in 1947, Americans United is a diverse and dynamic organization composed of people from all walks of life: lawyers and lobbyists, students and activists, religious leaders and impassioned Americans. Americans United includes people of faith and people who don’t profess any particular faith.

For nearly 80 years, we have litigated church-state issues in federal and state courts across the country, with a substantial practice before the federal courts of appeals and the U.S. Supreme Court. Most of our cases involve novel, cutting-edge First Amendment and other constitutional issues. In recent years, for example, we have litigated lawsuits and submitted amicus briefs challenging or opposing:

  • Coercive religious practices in the public schools.
  • Proselytizing by Trump-Vance Administration officials.
  • Public funding of religious education.
  • Religion-based refusals by businesses, foster-care agencies, and government officials to provide services to LGBTQ+ people and religious minorities. 
  • Religion-based efforts to deprive people of access to abortion and contraceptives. 
  • Race-based and sex-based employment discrimination by religious employers.

For more information about Americans United’s legal program, please visit our website at .

Duties and responsibilities. Legal interns receive substantive legal experience with in-depth exposure to some of the most important issues facing the nation. Interns assist with ongoing litigation by conducting legal and factual research and writing, analyze potential new litigation, and draft demand letters to resolve constitutional violations without filing suit. Interns may also draft pleadings, briefs, or discovery.

Our attorneys endeavor to prepare interns for public-interest legal practice, including by providing training and practical experience, in house and in conjunction with partner organizations. Interns are encouraged to take full advantage of the many events that take place in Washington, D.C., or are available virtually.

Eligibility and requirements. Law students (any year) who are committed to advancing the public interest and the separation of religion and government are encouraged to apply. Americans United includes and welcomes people of all genders, races, ethnicities, religions and beliefs, sexual orientations, gender identities, ages, socioeconomic backgrounds, and abilities. Because we work on a wide variety of issues and with many different communities, we value what diversity and diverse perspectives bring to our work.

Research shows candidates from marginalized groups are less likely to apply for positions when they don’t meet 100% of the listed requirements; please consider applying even if you don’t match 100% of these criteria.

Equal opportunity employer. Americans United is an equal opportunity employer. We consider applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, marital or veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected status. If you need an accommodation for a disability to apply to this position, please let us know by emailing . 

Compensation: A stipend of $7,360 for a ten-week term.

Work Location: Interns can work remotely from anywhere in the United States. There may also be opportunities to work in person in our Washington, D.C. office.

Working conditions and physical requirements. This position primarily involves working from a home office and/or professional office environment. The position requires routinely using standard office equipment such as computers, phones, and video-conferencing tools. It also requires the ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods, communicate effectively, and occasionally move about within the workspace.

How to apply.Please submit a cover letter, resume, law-school transcript, writing sample, and a list of three references through our web-based application portal at . The cover letter should highlight why you want to work with us and what perspectives you would bring to strengthen our practice. The writing sample may be of any length; it should be your best example of comprehensive and detailed legal argument or analysis, should be your own work, and should not be substantially edited by anyone else. First-year law students who apply before receipt of their initial grades may submit a law-school transcript that shows their initial courses and an undergraduate transcript. If you have any questions about an internship position, please do not hesitate to contact us at .

Deadline: Positions will remain open until filled. Applicants are encouraged to apply by October 15, 2026.

Salary: A stipend of $7,360 for a ten-week term

jobs.excerpt: CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country.
jobs.description:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.

We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.

We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.

About the Role

Location: Remote, United States

Role Type: Full-Time

Reporting to: Director of Business Operations

Compensation: $110,000 to $150,000 per year

We're mid-rollout of Claude Enterprise company-wide with Anthropic, and we want AI-first, human-in-the-loop workflows in every function where it makes sense, with agents doing meaningful recurring work. CodePath is hiring a Senior AI Operations Lead to drive that work across the organization. This job is as much about people and operations as it is about technology. Claude and the tools around it are powerful in skilled hands, and your mission is to build things with teammates that genuinely excite them and accelerate our mission of reprogramming higher education.

You operate as an internal consultant. You embed with a team, learn how they work today and how they want to work in the future, and translate that ambition into workflows, scheduled tasks, agents, and quality standards that hold up in production over time. Along the way you spot opportunities, connect dots across teams, and invent ways of working that did not exist.

We run enablement in layers, from onboarding to an internal community to open office hours to function-specific curriculum we co-develop with each team. This role is the deepest layer, and likely the most important: you sit with a team, build the workflow alongside them, and stay until it holds, which is how AI fluency turns into changed behavior and real impact.

This role may grow to lead a small team of embedded enablement specialists as the function scales.

What You'll Do

  • Embed and audit. Rotate through functions. Audit how the team really works, map the repetitive tasks, and find the highest-leverage opportunities
  • Build the v1 fast. Develop task-specific agents and automations (research synthesis, status updates, partner reporting, monitoring) using whatever ships fastest: Claude, Claude Code, MCP integrations, and our existing stack including Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, Asana, HubSpot, Zendesk, and internally developed tools. You ship something for feedback in hours
  • Productionize and set the quality gates. Default AI output drifts toward mediocrity over time. You turn rough prototypes, yours and your colleagues', into production-grade tools, with the rubrics, evals, and review steps that keep output at a standard the team can trust
  • Build reusable assets. Create the skills, plugins, and templates teams self-serve from after your engagement ends, and maintain them as the tools evolve
  • Coach to self-sufficiency. The goal of each engagement is a team that no longer needs you. You teach through building alongside people, meet them where they are in their AI proficiency, and leave each team more capable and more confident
  • Measure, report, and rotate on. Track outcomes like time saved and quality gained, not platform activity. Present results to leadership to prioritize the next engagement, then document what you built, hand off cleanly, and move to the next function

Requirements

  • 5+ years in automation/ops tooling, including recent hands-on LLM/agent work in a professional setting
  • Hands-on experience building with LLM tools and low-code/no-code automation platforms (e.g. Claude, n8n, Zapier, Make). Comfortable writing and iterating prompts and evaluating whether AI outputs are reliable enough to hand off to a non-technical team
  • A systems thinker who sees a 12-step manual workflow and immediately knows which 8 steps can be automated, and how seemingly disconnected pieces connect
  • Ability to embed with non-technical teams, earn trust quickly, and translate pain points into working solutions
  • Taste and judgment about quality. You can tell strong AI-assisted work from slop, and you know how to build the guardrails that keep it strong
  • Clear written and verbal communication. The range to meet anyone where they are, from a teammate opening Claude for the first time to someone who has been building their own workflows for months, and to move each of them forward

Preferred

  • Experience deploying Claude or another enterprise AI assistant across a largely non-technical organization
  • Familiarity with MCP integrations and agent architecture patterns
  • A background in change management or internal transformation programs

What This Role Is Not

  • A software engineer. You will not build infrastructure or ship product code. You automate business processes and build agents that make teams more effective and impactful
  • Purely a trainer. You will teach constantly, but you teach through building alongside the teams
  • A researcher. You evaluate tools when it serves an engagement, but the core of the job is building, deploying, and iterating

Compensation

CodePath standardizes salaries by level, no matter where you live. Salary within this band is determined by the relevant experience and skills you demonstrate through our interview process.

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a 100% remote position, work from anywhere in the U.S. CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 to Jan 2)
  • Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support
  • Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt
  • Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

jobs.description:
About Rebrandly

Rebrandly is a link intelligence and analytics platform that helps businesses create, share, and track branded short links, so marketing teams can see which campaigns actually drive results, not just clicks. Businesses use Rebrandly to keep their branding consistent across every link they share, whether it's in a social post, text message, or QR code. It also gives them visibility into how those links are performing and who's clicking them.

Rebrandly is a fully remote company with employees across the US and Europe, and our platform is trusted by millions of users worldwide, including global brands like Versace, Toyota, PayPal, and Zillow.

About the Role

Reporting to the VP of Product, you will work with the Growth Product Feature team. We have a large self-serve business with a traditional product-led growth motion.

You'd own PLG motion end to end: getting new signups to the point where the product is genuinely useful to them, turning that into paid, and spotting the accounts that have outgrown self-serve so our sales team can talk to them while they still care. We're not looking for someone who just runs the funnel as it exists today; we want someone who looks at it and sees the three different funnels we haven't tried yet. Your main number is self-serve conversion growth (signup → activated → paid). New self-serve MRR is the business outcome; conversion is what you're accountable for moving.

Compensation: $150k - $180k (if in USA)

Location: Remote, USA (East Coast time zone strongly preferred), Ireland, Canada (non-Quebec)

Rebrandly does not sponsor work authorization needs; candidates must have proper work authorization to work in the United States, without sponsorship.

What you'd work on first

  • Focus on Activation and Signups, turning into engaged users, turning into customers.
  • Finding the accounts worth a conversation with sales.

How we'd want you to work

  • Gather your own data. We have a strong foundation across our data warehouse, Metabase, Mixpanel, and MCPs to connect everything to Claude. We are looking for someone who can navigate the data fluently without a lot of support. You'll have more to work with than you might expect! A lot of useful data is accessible and the engineering team is strong and can deliver well. We have modern tooling and strongly embrace AI. Much of what you will need to be successful is already in place.
  • Think big, validate fast. We want bold ideas: a reimagined onboarding flow, a genuinely different pricing test, a new way of routing high-intent accounts to sales, tested in whatever way gets you a real signal fastest, not the most polished one. Twenty hand-picked accounts emailed to a rep can validate a routing idea before you'd ever finish building a scoring model. This is about speed of learning, not smallness of scope: we'd rather have a messy signal on a big idea in three weeks than a clean one in three months.
  • You own the roadmap and prioritization of what will create conversion activity and drive real revenue for the business.
  • Stay close to real users. Replays, support tickets, a few conversations a month. The data will tell you where people get stuck but almost never why.

What you need

  • 3-5 years of experience supporting a PLG/self-service product where you owned the success of conversion to paid
  • 3–5 years across product and growth work in a SaaS company, with a track record of ideas that were genuinely new, not just the next iteration on what was already there (bonus points if you have experience in Martech)
  • Fluency in website, demand-generation, and product-marketing launch practices; you know how a launch actually ships, what makes a landing page convert, and how to work with those teams. This matters more to us than technical depth; you need to have experience partnering with Marketing on growth levers
  • You can write. Upgrade prompts, value messaging, and pricing copy are growth levers
  • Enough comfort with product analytics and data manipulation to be self-sufficient; SQL fluency is a nice-to-have, not a requirement
  • Willingness to work in revenue numbers as well as product events

What you don't need

  • Paid or SEO expertise. That sits with our marketing team
  • Data modeling or dbt. You'll query the warehouse, not build it
  • Management experience. This is an individual contributor role for the foreseeable future

If you're strong on most of this and thin on one piece, apply anyway and tell us which piece.

Why Join Our Team:

  • Rebrandly provides its full-time US employees with comprehensive benefits, including:
    • Uncapped, flexible PTO
    • Enjoy your birthday off as a floating holiday
    • Company winter holiday closure the week between Dec 25- Jan 01

    • HSA, FSA, and supplemental life insurance options available

  • Annual professional development budget for continued learning

Availity is seeking a Chief Information Security Officer to lead the company’s enterprise cybersecurity, security assurance, and technology risk programs.   • Experience with AI security and governance, acquisition integration, and security teams distributed across the United States and India.

What you will be doing:

Enterprise cybersecurity leadership

  • Develop and execute a multi-year cybersecurity strategy aligned to business strategy, customer commitments, technology direction, and risk tolerance.
  • Set the enterprise security vision, priorities, policies, standards, operating model, and accountability across technology, product, engineering, business, and corporate functions.
  • Ensure security is built into application development, cloud architecture, data platforms, APIs, AI capabilities, and other core technology capabilities.

Security assurance, audits, and continuous compliance

  • Own Availity’s enterprise security audit and assurance strategy, including continuous readiness for customer, external, regulatory, and internal audits.

Board and executive engagement

Position Summary

The Procurement Director leads the execution and continued development of the enterprise procurement and vendor management function. The role owns procurement strategy, category planning, strategic sourcing, complex commercial negotiations, supplier governance, and procurement performance reporting, while ensuring alignment with business priorities, financial objectives, risk requirements, and company policies.

Working closely with business leaders, Legal, Finance, Information Security, Risk, and operational teams, the Director converts business demand and spend insights into actionable sourcing plans, measurable savings, stronger supplier performance, and timely contract outcomes. The role also provides day-to-day leadership, coaching, and prioritization for Procurement team members.

Key Responsibilities

Procurement Strategy and Category Leadership (25%)

  • Execute the annual procurement plan, category strategies, sourcing pipeline, and savings roadmap in alignment with business and financial priorities.
  • Use spend, market, supplier, and demand analysis to identify consolidation, cost optimization, competitive sourcing, and contract improvement opportunities.
  • Establish sourcing approaches and negotiation strategies for key IT, software, cloud, telecom, Hardware and operational categories.
  • Advise senior leadership on market trends, procurement risks, commercial options, investment trade-offs, and supplier strategies.

Strategic Sourcing and Commercial Leadership (30%)

  • Lead high-value, complex, and business-critical sourcing engagements from intake and market assessment through competitive process, negotiation, approval, and contract execution.
  • Direct RFIs, RFQs, and RFPs; establish evaluation criteria; facilitate stakeholder scoring; conduct commercial analysis; and present recommendations and business cases to decision-makers.
  • Lead negotiations with strategic suppliers on pricing, service levels, liability, risk allocation, implementation commitments, renewal protections, and other key commercial and contractual terms.
  • Partner with Legal and control functions to resolve complex issues, document risk-based recommendations, and escalate material decisions to the appropriate executives.
  • Oversee renewals, amendments, change orders, and Statements of Work to ensure commercial value, clear deliverables, acceptance criteria, and appropriate governance.

Governance Vendor Risk and Performance (20%)

  • Own procurement policies, approval standards, sourcing and contracting playbooks, and compliance controls; monitor adoption and address process gaps.
  • Ensure supplier onboarding, due diligence, and contracting activities are coordinated with Legal, Information Security, Risk, Finance, and other required reviewers.
  • Follow the risk-based vendor governance and performance framework, including service reviews, scorecards, remediation plans, executive escalation, and renewal decisions for critical suppliers.
  • Maintain visibility into key contract obligations, renewals, concentration risks, service issues, and commercial exposures, and provide clear recommendations to leadership.

Operations Analytics and Transformation (15%)

  • Own the procurement engagement tracker, contract pipeline, renewal calendar, spend reporting, and leadership dashboards, ensuring data is accurate, timely, and decision-useful.
  • Define and report procurement KPIs, including savings and cost avoidance, cycle time, sourcing activity, contract completion, renewal readiness, supplier performance, and onboarding progress.
  • Drive process improvement through workflow redesign, automation, standardized templates, user guidance, and effective use of source-to-contract, CLM, ERP, and reporting tools.

Team and Stakeholder Leadership (10%)

  • Lead, coach, and develop Procurement team members; allocate work, set priorities, review quality, and build consistent sourcing, contracting, analytics, and stakeholder-management capabilities.
  • Build trusted relationships with business leaders, clarify procurement accountabilities, and ensure stakeholders receive timely, practical, and commercially sound support.
  • Represent Procurement in cross-functional governance forums and lead supplier executive engagements, QBRs and escalations when required.

Qualifications and Experience

  • 12 or more years of progressive experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, vendor management, or commercial contracting, including leadership of complex and high-value engagements.
  • Demonstrated people leadership, coaching, work allocation, and quality oversight experience; formal team-management experience is strongly preferred.
  • Strong experience negotiating IT agreements, including SaaS, AI, cloud, hardware, telecom, and professional services, as well as operational supplier agreements.
  • At least five years of procurement experience in financial services, with sound understanding of third-party risk, governance, privacy, information security, and regulatory considerations.
  • Proven ability to develop category strategies, lead competitive sourcing events, build executive-ready business cases, and deliver measurable savings and cost avoidance.
  • Strong commercial judgment and working knowledge of contract structures, service levels, pricing models, liability allocation, implementation commitments, and supplier remedies.
  • Advanced analytical and financial skills, including spend analysis, forecasting, total-cost-of-ownership analysis, benchmarking, and executive dashboards; advanced Excel proficiency is expected.
  • Excellent executive communication, influencing, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to make clear recommendations and manage competing priorities.
  • Experience with CLM, ERP, source-to-contract, or procurement platforms such as GEP, Coupa, SAP Ariba, or Ivalua; experience implementing or optimizing these tools is an asset.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Finance, Law, or a related discipline is required. A relevant master's degree or professional designation such as SCMP, CPSM, or equivalent is an asset.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with stakeholders across North American time zones in a remote working environment.

Leadership Profile

  • Strategic and commercially minded, with the ability to translate business objectives into executable procurement priorities.
  • Decisive and accountable, with sound judgment on when to resolve issues independently and when to escalate material risk.
  • Analytical, organized, and execution-focused, with strong attention to contractual, financial, and operational detail.
  • Collaborative and service-oriented, while maintaining appropriate challenge, governance, and negotiation discipline.

About MFSG – Our Commitment to Responsible Innovation

At MFSG, we are committed to building innovative solutions grounded in ethical, transparent, and responsible use of data and technology. Aligned with the principles outlined in Canada’s Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA), we take a proactive approach to ensuring that any AI or data-driven systems we use are safe, fair, and accountable.

Position Summary:

The Portfolio Manager oversees the servicing and ongoing management of SBA, USDA, and conventional loan portfolios, ensuring full compliance with lender policies and agency regulations. This role analyzes credit risk, conducts annual reviews and servicing actions, supervises credit analysts, and facilitates communication among borrowers, lenders, and third parties, supporting loan modifications, monitoring, and documentation to protect agency guarantees and maintain portfolio performance. This position is jointly responsible for effective interaction with team members, lenders, and borrowers.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Provide excellent and professional customer service to the borrower, lender, and governing agencies. Ensure relationships remain strong and healthy.
  • Supervise Servicing Credit Analyst (including Decimal Point), review all financial spreads and narratives prepared by them, and ensure quality assurance of SBA/USDA credit files prior to audits and regulatory reviews.
  • Review borrower service requests, gather necessary information, and underwrite servicing actions—including modifications, annual loan reviews, and amendments such as collateral releases, pricing adjustments, risk-rating changes, and other necessary modifications—in accordance with lender policies, agency regulations, SOPs, and CFR.
  • Manage all aspects of portfolio management for SBA, USDA, Main Street, and conventional loans according to lender credit policy and SBA/USDA procedures, including portfolio monitoring, collections on past due accounts, collection of financial documentation, annual reviews, servicing actions, and communication with the SBA/USDA.
  • Collaborate with legal counsel, lenders, borrowers, and third parties on credit actions and servicing requests, including loan modifications, annual reviews, and documentation exception management; engage with all parties both verbally and in writing.
  • Complete comprehensive narrative annual reviews for each existing SBA/USDA loan, including business and personal financial analysis, credit analysis, lien perfection, property valuation, industry comparisons, risk identification and mitigation, and loan grading recommendations.
  • Order and review third-party reports such as real estate appraisals, environmental assessments, title reports, and business equipment valuations as required.
  • Ensure proper implementation of LSP, lender, and SBA/USDA business policies and procedures, and promote adherence to regulatory compliance requirements.
  • Maintain and manage financial and insurance ticklers, collect statements and policies, prepare SBA/USDA loan files for regulatory or agency audits, and fulfill all portfolio management responsibilities—including collections and communications between the lender and the SBA/USDA, and oversight of portfolio management expenses.
  • Participate in special projects and support the SBA/USDA servicing department as needed, including assisting borrowers with servicing actions and tracking financial, insurance, and covenant requirements.
  • Oversee the transition of a troubled loan to the Special Asset Portfolio Manager’s portfolio. Provide on going assistance as needed.

  • Continue to improve individual performance, with a goal of processing 9-12 actions a month

Education and/or Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting preferred.

Knowledge and/or Skills:

  • Knowledge of the SBA and USDA rules and regulations, preferred.
  • Strong credit skills.
  • Leadership and motivational skills, good written and verbal communication skills, decision-making and analytical skills and ability to work well under pressure.

Mathematical Skills:

Reasoning Ability:

jobs.description:
Symmetrio is recruiting an Integration Analyst for our customer, a growing healthcare technology organization focused on solutions that support radiation oncology and clinical care teams.

This individual will be responsible for designing, building, testing, and supporting healthcare integrations connecting clinical software platforms with electronic medical records (EMR) and oncology information systems. The role will work across HL7, FHIR, REST APIs, interface engines, cloud infrastructure, and clinical data workflows to ensure accurate and reliable exchange of patient and treatment information.

The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on experience with healthcare interfaces, data mapping and transformation, and troubleshooting complex integration issues across multiple systems. This individual will also work directly with hospital and healthcare IT teams during implementations, testing, and production go-lives.

This is a fully remote position within the United States, with occasional travel of approximately 10–15% to customer sites for onboarding and go-live support.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, configure, and support HL7 and FHIR interfaces connecting healthcare applications with EMR and clinical information systems.
  • Analyze source and target data models and develop detailed mapping and transformation logic for clinical and treatment data.
  • Build and maintain interface engine configurations using platforms such as Mirth Connect, Rhapsody, Cloverleaf, Corepoint, or similar technologies.
  • Troubleshoot interface failures, malformed messages, acknowledgment errors, mapping issues, and data integrity problems by tracing transactions across the full integration path.
  • Develop and maintain interface specifications, data mapping documentation, test plans, and technical runbooks.
  • Support integration services running in AWS and containerized environments, including Kubernetes and Docker, while monitoring logs, metrics, and system health.
  • Plan and execute unit, integration, and user-acceptance testing to validate data accuracy and system functionality prior to production deployment.
  • Collaborate directly with hospital and healthcare IT teams, implementation teams, software engineers, product teams, and third-party integration resources during customer onboarding and go-live activities.
  • Develop reusable integration templates, mapping standards, and implementation practices to improve the consistency and efficiency of future customer integrations.
  • Support clinical data integrations while maintaining appropriate handling of protected health information (PHI) and healthcare compliance requirements.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in healthcare interface or integration engineering, ideally within EMR, oncology, imaging, or other clinical technology environments.
  • Strong working knowledge of HL7 v2.x messaging, including ADT, ORM, ORU, and SIU messages.
  • Familiarity with HL7 v3/CDA, FHIR R4, and RESTful APIs.
  • Hands-on experience building or supporting integrations with major EMR platforms, particularly Epic; exposure to Cerner or similar systems is also valuable.
  • Experience with healthcare interface engines such as Mirth Connect, Rhapsody, Cloverleaf, Corepoint, or similar platforms.
  • Strong experience with clinical data mapping and transformation across disparate systems, including coded values, units, identifiers, and other healthcare data elements.
  • Working knowledge of AWS and containerized environments, including Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills with the ability to read logs, trace messages end-to-end, and identify root causes across multiple systems and teams.
  • Experience with scripting languages such as Python or JavaScript is preferred.
  • Familiarity with DICOM and healthcare imaging workflows is preferred.
  • Experience with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code technologies is preferred.
  • Experience with oncology, radiation oncology, treatment planning, or clinical workflow systems is highly preferred.
  • HL7, FHIR, AWS, or other relevant technical certification is a plus.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical field is preferred.
  • Ability to work core U.S. business hours, with occasional early or late meetings to collaborate with international engineering teams.
  • Willingness to travel approximately 10–15% to customer sites.

Benefits

  • Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
  • Retirement Plan (401k, IRA)
  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays)

jobs.description:
Sprinto is an Autonomous Trust Platform that centralizes trust requirements across security frameworks, vendors, and customers.

Sprinto autonomously executes tasks needed to maintain trust across compliance, audits, risk management, vendor risk, privacy, and AI governance, enabling organizations to maintain a strong, reliable trust posture without draining operational bandwidth and resources on repetitive tasks.

Backed by top-tier investors such as Accel, Elevation, and Blume Ventures, we’ve raised$31.8M in funding to fuel our mission. Trusted by over 4,000 organizations across 75 countries, Sprinto helps organizations stay audit-ready, manage real-time risks, and scale fearlessly. With 300+ native integrations and AI-driven automation, Sprinto supports 200+ global security standards natively, including SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and more. Sprinto's extensible architecture enables organizations to build and support an infinite number of custom integrations and frameworks.

Founded in 2020 by second-time founders Girish Redekar and Raghuveer Kancherla, Sprinto powers compliance for organizations like Whatfix, Encora, Anaconda, Whatnot, Ultrahuman, WeWork, Everstage, AI Foundation, HackerRank, and many more.

Life as a Sprinter -

Nobody succeeds at Sprinto by staying in their lane.

We are organized around problems, not job titles. Sprinters take ownership beyond their role, solve hard problems, and care deeply about the impact they create. If something can be improved, fixed, or built, we don't wait for permission; we step in.

Being remote means we rely less on proximity and more on trust. We write things down, communicate openly, and move quickly because great teams aren't built by sitting together, they're built by pulling in the same direction.

We believe progress beats perfection, feedback is a gift, and doing the right thing matters, even when nobody is watching.

And while we move with urgency, we never move alone.

The mission -

Where you'll leave your mark?

  • Own quality outcomes, not activities — the question is never "how many test cases did you write this sprint," it's "what quality metric moved and what did you build to move it."
  • Drive CI pass rate to 90%+ and keep it there — the percentage of pipeline runs that pass without manual intervention.
  • Own bug leakage rate — target under 2–3% of bugs escaping QA to staging or production, with a root cause analysis you own for every bug that gets through.
  • Build the system that keeps flaky tests out of the suite — preventing flakiness from entering and quarantining it when it does.
  • Shape automation coverage at the right layer — E2E where it matters, API where it's faster and more reliable, unit where developers should own it — not just chasing a coverage percentage.
  • Stay 50–60% hands-on — writing Playwright TypeScript to evolve the framework, building diagnostic tools that analyse test-run data for flakiness patterns, and reviewing PRs to catch structural problems in AI-generated test code.
  • Build AI-native quality infrastructure — systems that use LLMs, agents, and AI tooling to solve quality problems at scale, like pipelines that auto-analyse every PR for risk across security, product, and UX dimensions.
  • Deliver engineering-wide quality impact — at least one initiative per quarter that changes how developers or PMs ship, not just how QA tests. Our current guardrail system prevents 90 bugs per month without manual QA; that's the bar.
  • Partner and present — sit with product engineers to define quality gates before features ship, and present quality metrics (CI pass rate, bug leakage, flaky test trends) to engineering leadership.

The kind of builder we're looking for -

  • An engineer who has chosen quality as their specialisation — this is not a pure coding role and not a management role; it lives exactly in between (~40–50% strategy, cross-functional collaboration, and mentoring).
  • Engineering-wide in scope, not QA-internal — you want to improve how the entire engineering organisation thinks about quality, not just how the QA team works.
  • AI-native, not AI-assisted — you don't just use Copilot for test authoring; you build quality systems on LLMs and agents, and you can test AI features themselves — validating agent behaviour, checking LLM output quality, and handling non-deterministic systems.
  • A test pyramid thinker, not just an E2E automator — with developers now writing feature automation themselves, you push testing responsibility to the developer layer while QA owns integration, workflow, and AI feature quality. A candidate who only thinks Playwright and E2E is too narrow.
  • Fluent in the modern stack — Playwright, TypeScript, CI pipelines, and the data behind them.
  • Comfortable influencing without authority — defining quality gates with product engineers and changing developer behaviour through systems, not mandates.

How we care for our Sprinters?

  • Work wherever you are: We are 100% remote, so you get to choose if you want to work from home, a cafe, the hills, or the beach.
  • Co-working, on the house: If co-working is your jam, we offer a generous annual allowance.
  • We care about your learning: We are invested in seeing you grow and commit USD 1,000 annually to help you level up your skills.
  • We count your spark, not your leaves: Unlimited leave so you can reset when you need to.
  • Your Safety Net, Woven In: Health insurance with coverage up to INR 10 lakh for you and your family, accident protection of an additional INR 10 lakh, and life insurance worth 3x your annual salary.
  • Workspace setup of your dreams: We chip in INR 35,000 to help you build a setup that works for you.


Inclusion & Diversity -

At Sprinto, talent, curiosity, and ownership matter more than where you come from. We hire people for the problems they can solve, the impact they create, and the way they help others succeed—not their background, identity, or personal circumstances. We believe the best teams are built when people with different perspectives come together around a shared ambition to build something meaningful.

We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a fair, inclusive, and accessible hiring process for everyone.

jobs.excerpt: This role is for someone who can earn trust inside U.
jobs.description:
This role is for someone who can earn trust inside U.S. government agencies and drive complex technical commitments to completion. We are looking for a hands-on operator who personally owns delivery, not someone who operates only as a governance or advisory layer.

Tomorrow.io's Customer Delivery and Operations team sits at the center of the company, connecting the Government and Enterprise business units to the technical organization. We own the full lifecycle of customer programs, from pre-sale technical engagement through post-sale delivery and operational support. This role focuses on high-stakes U.S. government programs with defense, civil aviation, emergency management, homeland security, and other public-sector organizations.

You will own programs end to end. That means knowing the contract terms, technical requirements, acceptance criteria, stakeholder map, risks, and critical path. You will identify and resolve blockers early, close gaps between customer expectations and delivery, and maintain momentum across multiple engagements at the same time.

You will join a small, high-output team in a fast-moving company where the operating model is still maturing. There is no large program office behind you. You will build the frameworks and processes needed to execute and use them to keep programs moving.

What Winning Looks Like

  • Your programs deliver on time, within scope, and with zero surprises to leadership or the customer. Contract milestones are tracked, invoicing is clean, and required documentation and compliance artifacts are complete without being chased.
  • Government stakeholders in your programs trust you personally. Program leaders, contracting stakeholders, and technical counterparts come to you when something needs attention because you follow through consistently.
  • Internal teams in Science, Product, Engineering, Legal, and Finance treat your programs as well run and easy to support because you bring clear requirements, realistic timelines, and full context instead of last-minute fire drills.
  • You run multiple concurrent programs across different agencies, contracts, and compliance environments without dropping threads. Each program has a clear status, a clear next step, and a clear owner for every open item.
  • When a new U.S. government opportunity enters the pipeline, you step into the pre-sale engagement to support deal reviews, scope POCs, and ensure the technical, financial, and delivery picture is sound before we commit.
  • Risks surface early in your programs. You identify issues before they escalate and bring proposed mitigations with the diagnosis.
  • You raise the standard for the teams around you. Business Development teams produce stronger scoping because you challenge requirements and delivery assumptions before they reach the technical organization. Your programs become examples of well-run delivery.

What You Will Own

Program Delivery

  • Own and drive the full lifecycle of U.S. government programs, including contract kickoff, solution delivery, POC execution, operational deployment, and ongoing support.
  • Translate signed contracts and statements of work into executable program plans with defined milestones, deliverables, acceptance criteria, ownership, and accountability. Drive follow-through across all stakeholders.
  • Manage scope, schedule, budget, contractual commitments, and technical risk across multiple concurrent programs and agency environments.
  • Ensure all contract deliverables, including documentation, reporting, invoicing, and compliance artifacts, are completed accurately and on time.

Stakeholder Management

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for U.S. government customers on active programs. Build direct relationships with program leaders, contracting stakeholders, and technical counterparts.
  • Drive alignment across Legal, Finance, Product, Science, Engineering, Customer Success, and Business Development. Bring the right people together, resolve blockers, and maintain program momentum.
  • Navigate U.S. government acquisition processes, contracting norms, compliance requirements, and agency-specific decision paths with the confidence that comes from direct experience.
  • Manage relationships with prime contractors, subcontractors, integrators, and other external partners involved in delivery.

Pre-Sale Support

  • Support Business Development on active U.S. government opportunities by participating in deal reviews, validating POC scope, and ensuring the technical, financial, and delivery analysis is complete before commitments are made.
  • Bring an operational perspective into pre-sale conversations: what is realistic to deliver, what risks and dependencies exist, and what the program will require after award.
  • Contribute to proposal, RFP, RFQ, and RFI responses where credible execution planning is a differentiator.

Governance and Reporting

  • Report program health, risks, decisions, and progress to senior leadership on a regular cadence with clear, honest assessments.
  • Build and maintain program tracking, governance frameworks, and reporting standards that work for our scale and pace.
  • Provide clear guidance and governance support to cross-functional team members involved in program execution.

What You Must Bring

  • 8+ years of hands-on program or project management experience delivering complex technical programs for or with U.S. government customers. This must include direct delivery responsibility, not advisory or consulting roles where execution sat with another team.
  • Direct experience working with U.S. government agencies, ideally at the federal level, such as defense, civil aviation, emergency management, homeland security, or similar organizations. You understand government procurement and contracting because you have managed work within that environment.
  • A track record of personally owning and delivering programs end to end in environments without extensive institutional support. You have built the structures and processes needed to execute, not only operated within existing ones.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent programs across different agencies, contracts, and compliance environments without losing control of details or timelines.
  • Strong cross-functional influence skills. You have delivered through teams you do not manage, including Engineering, Science, Legal, Product, and Finance. You know how to align people, resolve conflicts, and create urgency without formal authority.
  • Excellent communication skills in English, written and spoken. You can write a clear program status, run a structured review, and communicate credibly with senior government officials.
  • Willingness to travel within the United States as programs require, with occasional international travel when needed. Although the role is remote, meaningful on-site presence is expected when customer relationships or program milestones demand it.
  • Eligibility for security clearance

Strong Plus

  • Experience with weather, climate, earth observation, or environmental monitoring technologies.
  • Familiarity with SaaS or Data-as-a-Service delivery models in a government context.
  • Familiarity with federal acquisition and contracting frameworks, including FAR and DFARS, and experience supporting RFP, RFQ, RFI, or other procurement paths.
  • Experience delivering through prime contractor, subcontractor, or systems integrator relationships.
  • Commercial acumen, including an understanding of deal economics, pricing structures, contract negotiation dynamics, and how delivery decisions affect margin.
  • Experience in a high-growth startup or scale-up environment where you built the operating model while running programs.

If you have reached this point and you are super excited but not sure you check all the boxes - we still want to speak with you! Your passion is priceless. Other things can be learned.
